title: Record verified Nanoleaf CI delivery alongside the merged guide refresh
body:
Companion to jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf#37 and merged source PR #61.

Add the verified source delivery record to guide maintenance history. Hub PR #89 merged the overlapping backlog/history refresh while this candidate awaited approval. Reconcile onto that main and preserve its inputs, generated HTML, architecture viewers, dates and Pixoo completion facts. The final comparison changes only updates.md. No product specification or UI delta remains.

The user approved the earlier guide candidate c2eb905. The reconciled candidate introduces no UI change relative to current main; regeneration is byte-identical. Guide build, maintenance regression and diff checks pass. Renewed independent reviews and all current-head CI remain required before guarded merge and main-CI verification.

Source #37 is verified at dd5005edf8bcdaf3a7b5d999fb1f5582d10ee0aa with all nine PR and main jobs passing. Its closure awaits this companion. Public website publication, installation and device actions are outside this source-only delivery.

title: Adopt planning and delivery checkpoints for the work guide
body:
## Change

Hub #83 adopts the guide checkpoints delivered by [agent-skills #33](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/33), source revision `ff80d247ea96a5d4c461d30a2c24148376197c7b`. Planning, candidate review, verified completion and authorized publication now lead to one Hub procedure. Reports distinguish source/tracker completion, guide synchronization, public publication and live verification.

Refresh the three paginated backlogs and merge histories, reconcile 111 primary open issues across 12 guides, and reference the completed external skill prerequisite without counting it as a device-project issue. The roadmap reflects the current Prism and Linux prerequisite sequences. The eight architecture viewers and their source evidence remain unchanged: this instruction adoption changes no device ownership, command path, transport or failure boundary. There is no product behavior or OpenSpec delta.

The read-only guide workflow uses the inspected job from separately owned PR #82. It builds offline, checks reproducibility and runs the browser checks; it grants no deployment access. PR #82, PR #84, Hub #73's reserved connector evaluation and Hub #80's initial hosting acceptance retain their owners.

## Validation

- Node 24, `npm ci`, `npm run check:workflow`, and `npm run test:workflow`: passed.
- `python3 docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py` and `python3 docs/work-guide/work/test_maintenance.py`: passed; 111 primary issues, 41 roadmap nodes, 46 merged PRs and eight viewers. Coverage initially rejected six newly open issues before their inputs were reconciled.
- `git diff --check`: passed. Nine HTML files inspected for public-content scope; no private machine-path, private-key or credential-token patterns found. Eight viewer hashes, architecture definitions, pins and receipts are unchanged.
- Local Chromium cannot launch under the host's socket restrictions. Current-head hosted browser/screenshots, all configured CI, independent Standards/Specification reviews and current-candidate human visual approval remain merge gates.
- Twenty-one source-backed instruction decisions passed across the three repositories, including three additional proposals-only cases at the final heads. Supplied skill paths establish simulated discovery only.

## Completion evidence

- Source/tracker: candidate for https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/83; do not close before all acceptance conditions are verified.
- Guide source: this PR; consumer companions are [Pixoo #56](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/pull/56) and [Nanoleaf #59](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/59).
- Public publication: pending separately supplied authority and exact merged Hub output after all main CI succeeds.
- Live verification: pending Pages deployment plus unauthenticated access and served-byte hashes for the landing page and all eight viewers.
- Next owner/action: delivery coordinator obtains remaining candidate evidence, performs guarded source merges, reconciles actual post-merge facts and prepares the public candidate. Source merge alone is not publication or physical acceptance.

GitHub currently refuses to start required CI because of an account payment/spending-limit restriction. The account owner must restore Actions availability, after which the coordinator will rerun the unchanged candidates. No CI, browser, merge or publication gate is waived.

Independent Standards and Specification reviews report no remaining P0–P3 findings at the final source comparisons: Hub `ddcc91543119eb60ed313cf5300b57de537ad64c`, Pixoo `76e681a36c5426d4ede538e7d83494e2d52da538`, Nanoleaf `2cb2d6d614d94b9207cf71f366c4033e6fcfd954`. The Pixoo provisioning pin defect was corrected and independently re-reviewed. Review requested Astra/high; instruction rehearsals requested Sol/high; executing identity/reasoning and coordinator reasoning are not independently exposed. No review waives CI, browser, human approval or publication acceptance.

[Delivery evidence and recovery steps](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/83#issuecomment-5611056705) record the final revisions, both independent reviews, 21 simulated instruction decisions, CI blockers and remaining source/guide/public/live stages.

title: Document the fresh Nanoleaf Linux runtime
body:
Documents the accepted fresh Nanoleaf installation in Ubuntu WSL. A new architecture diagram shows separate Linux hooks, CLI, wall map, controller and MCP processes coordinating through private Linux SQLite, with the on-demand worker as the sole light writer. The implemented Windows diagram remains available for comparison. Windows Desktop/browser clients and read-only mounted JSON remain in the proposed path.

Refs #43. Companion to [Nanoleaf source PR #57](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/57), owned by [Nanoleaf #54](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/54). [Nanoleaf #55](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/55) retains installed, actual-client and physical acceptance. Guide synchronization remains pending until this PR merges. Hub #43 remains open until the source, installation and documentation outcomes are complete.

Updates canonical architecture, roadmap, maintained guide inputs, pinned source receipts, generated HTML, the ninth interactive viewer and the dated maintenance record. The tracker snapshot and source-review timestamps stay distinct. The fresh install excludes data migration, rollback tooling, a combined daemon, a new hook API and shared monitoring. There is no Hub product behavior delta; the runtime specifications and ADR belong to Nanoleaf's archived `gh-54-linux-fresh-install` change. Concurrent Prism guide work in PR #82 retains its owner.

Validation:

- Archify passed all nine checks for each of nine diagrams. The new standalone viewer passed browser checks at four desktop sizes from 1440×900 through 2048×1320.
- `python3 docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py` and `python3 docs/work-guide/work/test_maintenance.py` passed: 12 guides, 110 primary issues, 117 linked issues, nine diagrams and 44 roadmap nodes.
- `node docs/work-guide/work/check_guide.cjs` passed with the documented installed-browser overrides. It checks widths 320–1440, navigation, links, search, diagrams and print behavior. Desktop, mobile and print captures were inspected.
- Guide SHA-256: `4d6f36fa10ae1206a5a6b63afb2a3928680980198b29e6a65cb0fdc737d5a1a7`. New viewer SHA-256: `24f1e34f94b532d178f12822eabfe0dba471d3c909a41f9ab4971691408721cf`.

Independent Standards and Specification reviews found no P0–P3 findings at base/merge-base `2564a357ec7d1a72c5525c0f36b98287244a6e89` and head `784ef8e40567da5a12a9cb9de273ff598da701f4`. See the [review receipt](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/84#issuecomment-5610851696). The existing work-guide user exemption in [Hub PR #76](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/76), retained in [Hub PR #79](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/79), removes only human approval for this document. All 24 current-head Hub push/PR jobs were refused before steps because of an account payment or spending-limit problem. Current-head checks must pass before merge. No installation, physical acceptance or public-site publication is claimed. The public guide remains unchanged until a separately authorized publication.

title: Document the Nanoleaf Prism delivery sequence
body:
The work guide now records the accepted Nanoleaf Prism sequence, connector geometry #52, crystal renderer #53, then luminous numbering #26. It distinguishes this sequence from the separately owned Linux installation and guide-artwork plans.

This is the source companion for [Nanoleaf PR #56](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/56), merged with all nine main jobs passing, and [renderer PR #58](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/58). Numbering #26 is in [PR #60](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/60) with passing local checks and independent review recorded. Its latest inherited visibility correction is receiving renewed review. Source delivery, human UI approval, installation and physical acceptance remain separate. Public guide publication is outside this delivery.

The paginated snapshot covers 114 open issues with one primary guide each, 121 linked issues, 48 roadmap nodes and 46 merged source PRs. Relative track headings prevent independent work from appearing to depend on the shared Codex milestone merely because it shares a column. Native dependency direction is preserved, including the full #54 → #55 → Hub #43 sequence in both the hosting table and roadmap. Newly planned Hub #83 and #85 through #87 are represented without implementing their work. Architecture definitions, pinned source receipts and the eight viewers are unchanged because Prism changes browser presentation without changing runtime ownership or command flow. Hub #73's reserved input stays untouched.

## Validation and review

At `bdac1f4ee27504063366b5c7ab2d0e162db97ee4`, the guide build, both maintenance tests and local browser checks pass. Chromium headless shell 149.0.7827.55 checked desktop, mobile, navigation, search, anchors, themes, diagram controls and print restoration. Screenshots and the print timeline were inspected. The HTML is 502224 bytes with SHA-256 `a7c9cc5c8482cb2bcf157656d7c00e82d502a90f440bc4771531841521ea40cd`. All 114 open issues have exact primary coverage. There were no runtime errors or guide external requests; the unchanged companion viewer rendered with its font request blocked and its fallback font available.

The added hosted guide job runs these existing checks and retains review artifacts without removing any existing job. Workflow validation passes three current specifications and three archives, plus ten workflow tests under Node 24.21.0. The refreshed native-dependency regression also covers the guide design/rollout chain and rejects a temporary reversed sequence. There is no product behavior or OpenSpec delta.

Fixed review comparison: base and merge-base `2564a357ec7d1a72c5525c0f36b98287244a6e89`, head `bdac1f4ee27504063366b5c7ab2d0e162db97ee4`, using `git diff BASE...HEAD`, with a clean worktree. Both renewed independent reviews are clear with no P0–P3 findings. All 13 configured current-head PR jobs passed: Checks run `34426914343` and Work guide run `34426914353`, both associated with PR #82 and this exact head. Current-candidate human UI approval, guarded merge and main CI remain required. Hosted execution has resumed; the guide keeps final Nanoleaf validation and source delivery pending and records the previous billing interruption as historical evidence.

Unavailable post-merge or issue-closure facts will be reconciled through a linked follow-up as the guide procedure requires. Guide synchronization remains pending until this companion merges.

title: perf: prepare real early source measurements; budgets pending
body:
Refs #30. Draft preparation for the early baseline/budget stage only. This is not an accepted early-stage delivery and does not release Hub #3.

The candidate measures real pinned Nanoleaf SQLite admission with worker launch excluded, and both actual released lifecycle validators in a disposable external npm consumer. It retains raw WSL samples, source/archive/tool hashes, process and clock boundaries, repeated profiles and observed load/resource data. It adds reusable negative/timeout/provenance checks and a real released-package consumer check to the existing Linux/Windows Python matrix. Existing CI jobs remain required.

Local Node 24/Python 3.14 build, type, controller-contract, lifecycle, MCP, package and workflow checks pass. Performance checks cover 14 cases plus both real validators and modified-corpus rejection. Nine admission profiles and six validator profiles completed. These are observations, not product budgets.

Missing matched Windows measurements, actual hook-return/helper coverage and frozen numeric budgets block early delivery. WSL interop still fails a version-only PowerShell probe with `UtilBindVsockAnyPort:307: socket failed 1`. The active OpenSpec change `gh-30-shared-monitor-performance` remains unfinished and unarchived. No guide completion claim, merge, overall issue completion or dependent implementation is authorized by passing tooling CI.

No installed clients, personal hooks/settings, live state, device operations or evaluation runs are included. Pinned upstream Python files are measurement inputs, not Hub provider implementations. The lifecycle archive is the real released 1.0.0 package, not a checkout-relative dependency.

Review corrections retain failing regressions for dependency shadowing and SQLite connection cleanup. Exact-byte Git attributes preserve pinned sources/receipts in Windows checkouts. All admission and validator profiles were rerun with their corrected tools; current candidate is `14c5f733cb48201014abea0e9043b1959e6690c6`. Both independent preparation reviews are clear; all twelve current-head PR jobs passed in run34289096133 and all twelve branch jobs passed in run34289093226. The early stage remains incomplete.

title: docs: plan PC and desk lighting integrations and backlog
body:
PC and desk lighting lacked a documented integration path and implementation backlog. Add a controller guide, architecture and roadmap links for Corsair RAM and supported H150i lighting, optional Lian Li Strimer, and the Varmilo VA108M-RGB keyboard. Preserve iCUE, L-Connect 3 and normal keyboard behavior, with one writer per lighting target.

Varmilo starts with whole-keyboard shared agent status through an existing supported interface. If none qualifies, its integration stays deferred. Per-key displays, custom protocol research, simulated keypress control and firmware replacement are excluded. Keyboard support does not block Corsair or Strimer delivery; Strimer does not block Corsair.

Refs #50. The eleven future skeletons #51-#58 and #60-#62 remain open for refinement before implementation. The existing guide #35 links them. Keyboard participation in shared status #55 and controls #56 conditionally requires #61, without making either shared issue depend on keyboard delivery.

## Validation

- Node 24.20.0: `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow` passed, including all 10 tests. Dependencies were installed with `npm ci` for the preceding documentation candidate; manifests and lockfile are unchanged.
- Checked 25 local Markdown links and `git diff --check`.
- Read back the updated issues and verified every native prerequisite relationship in their transitive graph in both directions: 29 issues, 52 edges, no cycles. Seven edges belong to the three new keyboard issues.
- Existing OpenSpec inventory: two capabilities, zero active changes and two archived changes, all applicable validation passed. This change has no product behavior or contract delta, so it introduces no OpenSpec change, runtime package, service or installation.

## Review comparison

Base and merge-base: `a7b1aa0476c2f3e0561b5d53dbc8395353180d60`.
Candidate head: `baf2b0bc2eb2b7839afe98175d8f3c686e5860c4`.
Diff: `git diff a7b1aa0476c2f3e0561b5d53dbc8395353180d60...baf2b0bc2eb2b7839afe98175d8f3c686e5860c4`.

Independent read-only Standards and Specification reviews both found no issues against this exact comparison. The worktree is clean. Standards review checked repository rules, ownership, contract and evidence boundaries, and the linked vendor/OpenRGB claims. Specification review reconciled both eleven-row documentation dependency tables against the issue graph and accepted scope.

## CI and device evidence

GitHub refused to start all eight jobs in each current-head workflow: [PR run](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/34176141304) and [branch run](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/34176139337). All sixteen jobs have zero executed steps. Annotations report failed account payments or a spending limit requiring an increase. This is an account execution blocker, not a failed test assertion.

Merge remains blocked by `AGENTS.md` and `docs/sdlc.md`. Resolve the GitHub billing/spending restriction, rerun both workflows, and refresh current base/head/reviews. Merge only after every configured job succeeds, using the guarded squash procedure. Verify all merged-revision main CI jobs before closing #50. No merge or account-setting change was performed.

Hardware evidence is limited to user-supplied model information, application screenshots, historical records and read-only generic Windows inventory. Keyboard automation compatibility remains unverified. Source, installation, real-client, transport, visible-light and typing/restoration evidence remain separate. This PR does not operate hardware or alter installed software.
